title: introduce-cost-sculptor-prescriptor-for-batching-cache-and-quant-defaults
author: Alyssa Chen
description:
Motivation: We need a compact, safer defaults engine that recommends batching, cache and quantization presets per workload profile to reduce per-token unit cost without manual tuning. This PR introduces 'Cost Sculptor' (internal name) - a prescriptor service and small console UX that suggests conservative defaults and optionally auto-applies them behind a feature flag. Context: large customers frequently under-tune batching/cache/quant settings and see high unit costs. Existing autotuners are aggressive and require long profile runs. Cost Sculptor provides quick, explainable presets computed from short sampling windows and historical telemetry.

What this PR does (summary): Adds a prescriptor microservice (pkg/econ/prescriptor) that consumes workload profiles and returns batching/cache/quant presets; exposes a REST endpoint and a CLI shim; wire the console to surface suggestions; adds an opt-in auto-apply rollout; records telemetry for applied suggestions and a light-weight A/B metric for unit cost delta.

Design notes: - Prescriptions are generated by a rule+heuristic engine (no ML model in this PR) with tunable thresholds to avoid regressions. - Safe fallbacks: suggestions include safety caps (max batch size, quant aggression limits) and a rollback window. - Telemetry: adds metric tags (suggestion_id, policy_version, candidate_profile) so we can measure impact and do experiments. - Feature flag: cost_sculptor.suggest_enabled and cost_sculptor.auto_apply for controlled rollout.

Checklist:
- [x] Core prescriptor engine and REST API
- [x] Console panel with suggestion preview + apply button
- [x] CLI shim for ops teams: redwoodctl econ suggest --sample <job>
- [x] Integration tests including simulated workloads
- [x] Telemetry and event schema registration
- [x] Docs: docs/operator/cost-sculptor.md and quickstart
- [x] Feature-flag gating and rollout plan

How to test locally: 1) run `make dev-prescriptor` which brings up prescriptor on :8089; 2) run sample generator scripts/scripts/sample-workload.sh to produce a short profile; 3) curl POST /v1/prescribe with the profile or use `redwoodctl econ suggest`; 4) in console -> Advanced -> Cost Suggestions you can preview and apply. See tests/e2e/cost-prescriptor.spec.ts for end-to-end smoke tests.

Bench summary: On a 7-day sampled trace from a mid-market customer (mixed short/medium sequences): - Median token-cost reduction: ~18% (range 11-26%) - P95 tail latency increased < 2% in worst case when auto-apply used conservative presets - Quantization suggestions applied q4->q4f gave ~9% decrease in GPU memory and enabled 1.15x request throughput for small-medium sequences. Bench scripts are in scripts/eval-profiles.sh and results logged under tools/benchmarks/cost-sculptor/.

Rollout plan: Start behind suggest_enabled for all customers (UI visible) but auto_apply only for internal tenants. Stage: internal -> beta customers (by invite) -> gradual ramp controlled by metric unit_cost_delta and latency_95. We will monitor the rollback window flag and have a kill-switch in console.

Related: ENG-1982 (prescriptor MVP), ENG-2043 (telemetry schema for econ suggestions). See docs link: https://internal.redwood/docs/operator/cost-sculptor

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the prescriptor deterministic and conservative; a follow-up (ENG-2067) will add a learned ranking model and simulated A/B evaluation harness.

Priya Natarajan: UX looks good, but add copy for 'why we suggest this' (explainability).
Alyssa Chen: Added explanation panel and doc blurb. Priya approved.

Final reviewers: Samir (approve), Diego (approve after bench added), Priya (approve).

files_for_ops: configs/features.yaml (feature flags), docs/operator/cost-sculptor.md (runbook), scripts/sample-workload.sh (sampling), tools/benchmarks/cost-sculptor/ (bench results)
testing_instructions:
1) make dev-prescriptor && ./scripts/sample-workload.sh > /tmp/profile.json
2) curl -XPOST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' localhost:8089/v1/prescribe -d @/tmp/profile.json
3) In Console: Advanced -> Cost Suggestions -> Preview -> Apply (auto-apply gated by feature flag)
4) Validate telemetry appears under metric econ.suggestion.applied and econ.suggestion.rollback
5) Run tests: yarn test:e2e cost-prescriptor
notes_for_reviewers: Key risks: incorrect quant recommendations causing quality regressions; mitigations: conservative quant caps and rollbacks, explainability panel for operator review. Please focus on the telemetry schema and the safety short-circuits for latency-critical routes.
audit_trail: author: Alyssa Chen created 2024-11-07 -> pushed WIP commits -> requested changes from Samir/Diego -> added safety short-circuits and bench artifacts -> CI rerun -> approvals -> merged 2024-11-14
security_notes: No secrets are introduced. Prescriptions are suggestions only; auto-apply is gated by feature flag and requires operator consent in console for non-internal tenants. Telemetry events scrub route identifiers when privacy mode enabled.
observability_changes: Adds metrics: econ.suggestion.generated, econ.suggestion.applied, econ.suggestion.rollback, econ.suggestion.latency_delta; adds traces for /v1/prescribe endpoint; dashboard stub at observability/cost-sculptor.md
